paper_sections.title: Altered regional activity and connectivity of functional brain networks in congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss
3.2 Differences in regional activity and connectivity

description.value: The study examined regional spontaneous brain activity, seed-based functional connectivity, global-signal-regression effects, and associations with clinical variables in patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia and severe hearing loss compared with matched normal-hearing controls.

spans.text: To examine the effect of GSR on UM-related functional alterations, rs-fMRI data were analyzed both with and without GSR during preprocessing.

design.value: Resting-state fMRI case-control comparison between 24 patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia and 25 age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls, including ALFF, fALFF, ReHo, seed-based functional connectivity, and ROI-wise clinical correlations, analyzed with and without global signal regression.

description.value: Resting-state fMRI preprocessing included deletion of the first 10 time points, slice-timing and head-motion correction, normalization to the EPI template, resampling to 3-mm isotropic voxels, smoothing with a 4-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, nuisance regression, temporal band-pass filtering, and scrubbing.

spans.text: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted because of the instability of the initial MRI signal and the need for participants to adapt to the scanning environment. Thereafter, slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented. The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template, resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels, and further smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
